originalTitle: DOJ says it will not reopen criminal probe into former Fed Chair Powell
summary: The confirmation comes after the Fed's inspector general report that said there were no grounds for a criminal referral over the mismanaged headquarters renovation.
content:
The Department of Justice will not reopen its criminal investigation into former Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell over the central bank's overbudget multibillion-dollar headquarters renovation a department spokesperson told CNBC.

"We're not reopening a criminal investigation into him," Attorney General Todd Blanche told Bloomberg in an interview Friday.

Blanche did not rule out separate Justice Department action related to the renovation in his interview. He told the outlet the independent audit of the renovation could prompt an investigation if it uncovers evidence of criminal wrongdoing.

His comments come days after the Federal Reserve's inspector general found no reasonable grounds to believe that a federal crime had occurred requiring a referral to the attorney general, even as the watchdog faulted the central bank for major management and oversight failures that contributed to the project's soaring costs.

President Donald Trump slammed the decision, said in a Truth Social post Wednesday after the news, saying that Powell should be "forced to resign" from the central bank's Board of Governors "at a minimum."

"He can't manage a Building, and he certainly shouldn't be allowed to manage his High Interest Rate Policy (only on 'TRUMP!')," Trump said.

The Justice Department opened its investigation into the renovation in January. Prosecutors issued grand jury subpoenas seeking related records but a federal judge quashed those subpoenas in March, finding they had been issued for an improper purpose and that the government had produced essentially no evidence that Powell committed a crime. The DOJ disputed the ruling but later closed its investigation rather than appeal.

Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh , who succeeded Powell in May, said the central bank would bring in an independent auditor and strengthen oversight of the project. Powell remains on the Fed's Board of Governors, where his separate term runs through Jan. 31, 2028.

Trump has repeatedly pushed Powell to leave the board altogether after years of clashes over interest-rate policy.

CNBC's Ryan Ruggiero contributed to this report.
chineseTitle: 美国司法部表示不会重新启动对美联储前主席鲍威尔的刑事调查
chineseSummary: 这一确认是在美联储监察长报告称没有理由就管理不善的总部翻新工程进行刑事移交后做出的。
chineseContent:
司法部发言人告诉 CNBC，司法部不会重新启动对美联储前主席杰罗姆·鲍威尔 (Jerome Powell) 的刑事调查，该调查涉及美联储预算超支的数十亿美元总部改造工程。

“我们不会重新对他展开刑事调查，”司法部长托德·布兰奇周五在接受彭博社采访时表示。

布兰奇在采访中并未排除司法部就翻修工程采取单独行动的可能性。他告诉媒体，如果发现犯罪行为的证据，对翻修工程的独立审计可能会引发调查。

几天前，美联储监察长发现没有合理的理由相信发生了联邦犯罪，需要将其移交给司法部长，尽管监管机构指责央行存在重大管理和监督失误，导致该项目成本飙升。

周三消息传出后，唐纳德·特朗普总统在《真相社会》的一篇文章中猛烈抨击了这一决定，称鲍威尔“至少应该”“被迫”辞去央行理事会职务。

特朗普说：“他无法管理一座大楼，当然也不应该允许他管理他的高利率政策（仅限于‘特朗普！’）。”

司法部于一月份开始对翻修工程进行调查。检察官向大陪审团发出传票，寻求相关记录，但一名联邦法官在三月份撤销了这些传票，认为这些传票是出于不当目的而发出的，而且政府基本上没有提供鲍威尔犯罪的证据。美国司法部对裁决提出异议，但后来结束了调查而不是上诉。

五月份接替鲍威尔的美联储主席凯文·沃什表示，央行将引入独立审计员并加强对该项目的监督。鲍威尔仍担任美联储理事会成员，其任期将持续至 2028 年 1 月 31 日。

在多年的利率政策冲突后，特朗普多次敦促鲍威尔完全离开董事会。

CNBC 的 Ryan Ruggiero 对本报告做出了贡献。
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于财经市场信号，适合用于观察利率、汇率、股债商品、金融机构和宏观政策变化。
